title: The Knowledge Graph Mullet: Trimming GraphRAG Complexity - William Lyon
talk_summary: A vendor talk about Dgraph's hybrid property-graph/RDF model and GraphRAG, where vector search is only an entry point into a domain graph that is then traversed for richer context. The last third demos an MCP server for the database and a prompt-plus-MCP-connections agent builder with an 'eject to code' escape hatch.

takeaways.technique: Read-only vs. full-access MCP endpoints per service
takeaways.what_they_do: Each Dgraph instance exposes two MCP servers: a read-only one (query + schema inspection only) and a full one that also allows mutations and schema changes, so agents can be granted the least privilege they need.

takeaways.technique: Agent self-verifies writes via follow-up queries
takeaways.what_they_do: After generating mutations, the model issues queries to confirm the data matches expectations and patches missing relationships when it doesn't.

takeaways.technique: Prompt-defined agent with MCP connections, ejectable to code
takeaways.what_they_do: Agents are created from a prompt plus a set of MCP tool connections, and can be exported to the underlying open-source framework when more complex logic is needed.

takeaways.technique: Graph traversal as context expansion beyond vector hits
takeaways.what_they_do: Vector similarity finds seed chunks, then graph traversal through shared topics/entities pulls in related documents that vector search missed, as additional context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: traverse through the topic nodes to find other articles that have overlapping topics but that may not have shown up through our vector similarity search
